description: Authorized modifications to protected (baseline) surfaces and governance controls. Schema v2: every entry must be COMPLETE — id, phase, dates, requester {login,role}, rationale, risk, affected_functionality, new_functionality, regression_tests, evidence {summary,links}, changes[] with per-file content_sha256, and a structured tl_approval {approved:true, approver, date, decision_ref} whose approver is a baseline.governance.approvers login. entries.rationale: Deterministic repair of the inherited provider-stop integration test's admission race (final-closure handoff §12 regression discipline; the same authorized inherited-test-repair class as the M2-F trust-anchor rotation and the gamos-plan-acceptance fixture repair). CI run 42494215014 on merge commit 12ac5906 failed honestly: expected cancels ['ask#1','ask#2'], observed ['ask#1'] — the two ask request lines can land in two child-stdout chunks, the parent admits them in two ticks, and ask#1's stop-run action (scheduled on queueMicrotask) can fire before ask#2 is admitted, changing the cancellation set. The package's own testing vocabulary already solves exactly this class (AskAction submit.delayMs, documented: 'only a real time delta can pin the order' — resume.test.ts). (1) auto-driver.ts: extend delayMs to the stop-run action (additive optional field; same scheduling path; no behavior change for actions without delayMs). (2) provider-stop.test.ts: give the stop-run action delayMs 200 so both sibling asks are admitted and in-flight before the stop lands — the invariant under test (the cancellation set and the running-status journal rows) is then pinned by real time, not by chunk luck.

No production source, no engine surface, no runtime code path, no IPC/RPC channel, no contract document is touched. The 7 skip-vs-run Blender gate tests and every other suite in the package are unaffected (verified: full package suite 100 passed + 7 honest Blender skips, same as before the change).
entries.new_functionality: AskAction stop-run gains an optional delayMs (real-timer scheduling, identical semantics to the existing submit.delayMs) so tests that depend on admission order versus a run-level stop can pin the order deterministically. The provider-stop test uses it to close the CI-only flake.

tl_approval.decision_ref: Final-closure directive §12 (regression discipline: every CI-only failure is fixed at its root, honestly recorded, never retried away) + the package's own documented testing rule (AutoDriver header: only a real time delta can pin sibling-admission order). TL-reviewed: test-only change class; the optional delayMs field mirrors the existing submit.delayMs vocabulary; no production surface touched.
